idea: A tool that turns receipts into expense reports for freelancers.
why: Lena describes money and time already lost, a paid tool she cancelled, and commits to paying and to a date.
transcript:
Interviewer: We're building a tool that turns receipts into expense reports. How do you handle expenses today?
Lena: Every month I spend a full Saturday typing receipts into a spreadsheet.
Lena: Last quarter I missed 400 dollars in deductions because I lost receipts.
Interviewer: Have you tried anything else?
Lena: I paid 15 dollars a month for an expense app for six months.
Lena: I cancelled it because it could not read handwritten receipts.
Lena: I work mostly with small design studios.
Interviewer: We have a beta. Would you want to try it?
Lena: I will pay for a year upfront if it reads handwritten receipts.
Lena: Send me the link today.
Lena: I already put Friday at 10 on my calendar to move my receipts over.

idea: A browser extension that summarizes long email threads for managers.
why: Marcus is warm and encouraging but reports no problem, no past behavior and no commitment.
transcript:
Interviewer: We're building an extension that summarizes long email threads. How do you deal with them today?
Marcus: I just skim them.
Marcus: I manage a team of six.
Interviewer: Does skimming ever cause problems?
Marcus: Not that I can think of.
Interviewer: What do you think of the idea?
Marcus: That is a neat idea.
Marcus: I think a lot of people would like that.
Marcus: I would probably use it if it was free.
Interviewer: Would your team use it?
Marcus: I am sure they would love it.
Marcus: You should definitely build it.
Interviewer: Could we follow up next month?
Marcus: Sure, maybe.
